clips.title: The Apprenticeship
grammar: 〜てほしい — wanting someone to do something

lines.ja: ただ、がむしゃらに迷い続ける、若手芸人・徳永。
lines.en: Tokunaga, a young comedian blindly struggling along his path.
lines.speaker: Narrator

lines.ja: 俺の、伝記を作ってほしいねん。
lines.en: I want you to write my biography.
lines.speaker: Kamiya

lines.ja: 決して周りに媚びない、型破りな先輩芸人・神谷。
lines.en: Kamiya, an unconventional senior comedian who never sucks up to anyone.
lines.speaker: Narrator

clips.title: Unique Brand of Comedy
grammar: 〜節がある — to have a tendency to

lines.ja: それは個性とは言われへん。もう吠えやで。
lines.en: You can't call that originality. It's just barking.
lines.speaker: Kamiya

lines.ja: お前にしか作られへん笑いが、絶対あるんやで。
lines.en: There's definitely a comedy that only you can create.
lines.speaker: Kamiya

lines.ja: この人が全ての答えを持っていると思い込んでいる節が、僕にはあった。
lines.en: There was a part of me that assumed this man had all the answers.
lines.speaker: Tokunaga

clips.title: There Is No Bad End
grammar: まだまだ — still far from, not yet

lines.en: there's no such thing as a bad ending.
lines.speaker: Tokunaga

lines.ja: 僕たちは、まだまだ途中だ。
lines.en: We're still midway on our journey.
lines.speaker: Tokunaga
